text.p: General Motors Corp's Australian unit General-Motors Holden's Automotive Corp said on Friday it may have to upgrade up to 300,000 of its Commodore models after detecting potential transmission problems.
Holden spokesman John Morrison told Reuters the company had issued a recall notice for 120,000 vehicles fitted with an automatic transmission and tow bar built since July 1993.
However he said the company had also offered to upgrade another 180,000 vehicles without towbars, in the interests of any future towing use by the owner or subsequent owners.
"So we are actually doing more than we have to, extending the customer service...(but) the recall is very specifically directed at the 120,000 (vehicles) with towbars," he said.
Morrison said the costs of the upgrade were significant, but the company was prepared to release specific figures.

In its recall notice, Holden said it had received a small number of reports of transmission fluid leaking as a result of towing when the recommended transmission fluid cooling kit had not been fitted and/or recommended towing schedules were not followed.
